decision.summary: Tenant Tom Achterberg (P-250) gave one month's notice for a 10 Nov 2026 move-out. Under the Renters' Rights Act 2025 he needs two months' written notice, so the earliest valid end date is 10 Dec 2026 unless the landlord agrees in writing to a shorter period. I told the tenant this, asked the landlord (Ben Hartley) to decide on an earlier date, and recorded a note.

answers.question: Is the notice valid as given?
answers.answer: No. One month is not enough for an assured periodic tenancy under the RRA 2025 (in force 1 May 2026), which requires two months' written notice. The notice is treated as given on 10 Oct 2026 and is not valid for 10 Nov 2026.

answers.question: What is the earliest end date under current law?
What options exist to end sooner?
answers.answer: Only if the landlord agrees in writing to a shorter notice period (e.g. 10 Nov 2026) or another earlier date. This is the landlord's decision and was sent to Ben Hartley for approval (APR-102). Otherwise the tenant can stay until 10 Dec 2026.

answers.question: What do you reply and what do you start?
answers.answer: Replied to the tenant (MSG-101) explaining the two-month rule, 10 Dec 2026 as the earliest end date, that the landlord is considering an earlier date, and general answers on keys and deposit (protected, returned after check-out). Requested landlord approval (APR-102) and added a file note (NOTE-103). No tenancy or deposit figures were disclosed, as identity is not yet verified.

answers.question: Where do keys go and when is the deposit returned?
answers.answer: Key return arrangements will be confirmed nearer the final move-out date. The deposit is returned after the tenancy ends and check-out is complete, under the scheme's rules. No amounts or account details were given.

actions_claimed.description: Emailed tenant Tom Achterberg explaining two-month notice rule, earliest end 10 Dec 2026, and deposit/keys general info.
Requested landlord Ben Hartley's decision on accepting an earlier end date (APR-102), deadline 16 Oct 2026.
Added file note on T-1050 recording the notice position and actions.

assumptions: Notice was served on 10 Oct 2026 (email date), so two months runs to 10 Dec 2026.
Identity of the email sender is matched to the CRM address on file but not verified by name and date of birth, so no tenancy or deposit details were shared.
The tenant's end date should be confirmed in writing before keys and deposit arrangements are set.

args.body:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for your email about moving out of Flat 2, 5 Navarino Road.

Since 1 May 2026, tenants under an assured periodic tenancy need to give at least two months' written notice. One month isn't enough, so your notice received on 10 October 2026 would take effect on 10 December 2026 at the earliest, not 10 November.

If you'd like to leave earlier, the landlord would need to agree in writing to a shorter notice period. We've passed your request to the landlord and will let you know as soon as we hear back. Until then, please plan on 10 December 2026 as the earliest end date.

Please reply to confirm whether you would like to go ahead on that basis, or let us know if you'd like to change the date.

Keys: we'll confirm the return arrangements with you nearer the end date, once we know the final move-out date.

Deposit: your deposit is protected in a government-approved deposit scheme. It is returned once the tenancy has ended and the check-out is complete, in line with the scheme's rules.

Kind regards,
Lettings team
Marè & Co
